title: Strong and Surrendered
subtitle: Eight weeks. You already have a foundation — you stopped training it.

week_list.title: Showing Up
week_list.opening_line: The ask and the promise have been fused in your head for years, and that fusion is the reason you have quit eleven times.
week_list.stakes: Skip this week and you spend eight weeks performing — the hard sessions done, the boring ones skipped, and October arriving with better vocabulary and the same body. The cut corner starts here, on the first night nobody is counting.
week_list.pull_quote: Keep the promise, and the ask stops being a verdict on you.

blocks.v: The four shapes

blocks.label: Hollow
blocks.cue: Held from the middle. Nothing propping you up and nothing leaking out.

blocks.label: Arch
blocks.cue: The front of you open. Throat and chest exposed, chin lifted.

blocks.label: Stacked
blocks.cue: One line under load. Head over ribs over hips over heels.

blocks.label: Landing
blocks.cue: Feet down, knees soft, chin up. Absorb it and get up.

blocks.v: Two minutes. Every day. Fifty-six days. These four do not change and nothing gets added.

items.head: Low back flat
items.sub: Pressed into the floor. Put a hand under it first and feel the gap disappear.

items.head: Ribs pulled down, not flared
items.sub: This is where it goes wrong and you will not feel it happen.

items.head: Head and shoulders a few inches up
items.sub: Chin off the chest.

items.head: Feet a few inches up
items.sub: The instant the low back lifts, bend the knees or drop the feet until it is flat again.

items.head: Twenty seconds, twice
items.sub: A small honest hollow beats a big fake one, and that is true of most things.

blocks.title: What each shape is in you
rows: Holding yourself together on the day nobody claps
Asking for the big thing, and being able to take delivery of it
Your word holding from what you said down to what is true
What you do the day after you fall

blocks.v: Most women find arch harder than hollow. That tells you something before I say a word about it.
What has to be automatic first
Thirty logged days of daily practice. Recent evidence that you show up. Something to set a bad number against. Then the measurement stops being a verdict, and you write it down anyway.
No thirty days? Go and get them. That is not a delay. It is the first rung and you do not skip rungs.

items.head: Shapes drill
items.sub: Two minutes, all four, every day, before the session. Seven of seven.

items.head: Session A — The Six
items.sub: All six patterns, three rounds, light or bodyweight. This is the live one.

items.head: Session B — alone
items.sub: Same six patterns, same three rounds, later in the week, on your own.

items.head: Three walks
items.sub: Twenty minutes, conversational. Say a full sentence out loud to prove the pace.

items.head: One long stretch
items.sub: Twenty minutes, floor only. Breathe out longer than you breathe in.

items.head: Thursday — the baseline
items.sub: Warm up first. Five measures, one honest attempt each, written in ink.

blocks.title: The inner work — the ask and the promise

items.head: Five minutes, no writing
items.sub: Sit. Feet flat. Hands open on your thighs, palms up. Breathe out longer than in, ten times.

items.head: Ten minutes, writing
items.sub: Verbs only. What do I want to be able to do? Fill the page. No editing, no ranking.

items.head: Three minutes
items.sub: Read it back and circle the one that made your chest tighten. Not the most impressive one. The one that cost something.

items.head: Five minutes
items.sub: Turn it into a prayer and say it out loud, standing, in a room, with your voice.

items.head: Two minutes
items.sub: At the bottom of the page write the promise — thirty minutes, the time of day, the place.

items.head: Sign it
items.sub: With your name, like a document, because it is one.

blocks.title: The ask and the promise are not the same size

left.head: The ask
items: Big. Specific. Out loud, to God, unhedged.
A verb, never a picture. "I want to get off the floor without using my hands."
It costs something to say. Your chest tightens when you write it.
It is not a referendum on Tuesday.

right.head: The promise
items: Small. Thirty minutes. Today.
A time on a clock and a place.
Almost insultingly small, and the smallness is the mechanism.
Keep it, and the ask stops being a verdict on you.

blocks.v: When women pray about their bodies they almost never ask. They apologize. Lord, help me be more disciplined is a prayer about your character flaws, not a request. Ask for the thing. Use the verb.

blocks.title: The baseline — Thursday, one attempt each, no retakes
rows: From a chair, thirty seconds, counted, no hands
Hold until your hips drop, not until you decide to stop
At your honest level — counter, chair seat or floor
Note what your breathing is doing at minute nine
Get down and back up however you actually do it
Points of contact used — hands, knees, furniture

blocks.v: You will want to warm up secretly for three days first. That impulse is the thing we came here to dismantle. Write the number while your neck is still hot. Do not retake a single one.

blocks.text: Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much.
blocks.why: Here because this week is almost insultingly small, and little is the only site where trustworthiness has ever been built.

blocks.text: Your eyes saw my unformed body.
blocks.why: Whatever number you write on Thursday, it is not news to Him.

blocks.title: Done means
items: Seven daily entries logged — seven, not six
The shapes drill seven of seven, before the session
Thirty minutes or more of movement on each of those seven days
Two strength sessions, three walks, one long stretch, one your choice, all accounted for by name
Five baseline numbers in ink, no retakes
The promise page signed, with a time of day and a place on it
The ask said out loud, once, in a room, with your voice
blocks.demo: Hold a hollow for twenty seconds with your low back flat the whole time, and say the difference between the ask and the promise out loud without looking at the page.

blocks.title: Not every hard thing is a gap
blocks.v: Fresh grief, or old material arriving with your whole body attached, is not a cut corner and I will not pretend it is. Move your thirty minutes, log it, and take the rest to a licensed professional.

week_list.title: Strength Is a Moral Fact
week_list.opening_line: Being strong is a moral fact and not a vanity project, and the evidence for it is not in the mirror — it is in a notebook, in your handwriting, in ten-pound increments.
week_list.stakes: Skip this week and you keep the belief you walked in with, that fitness is a personality type and you are not it. And you arrive at week three with nothing in your hands to put where the contempt was.
week_list.pull_quote: Weakness is not a private matter. It gets outsourced, and somebody else has been paying.

blocks.v: What has to be automatic first
Seven days kept, not five. Five numbers on paper you did not retake. A body that already answers. The hollow findable without rehearsing the order. Now load can go on top.
Load goes on consistency. It does not go on intention. Four days last week? Run week one again for seven and come back. That is the ordinary Tuesday decision in every gym on earth.

Progressive overload is gymnastics progression with the childhood taken out of it. Same architecture — a little more than last time, and only once last time is automatic. It is what I used on myself for six years to get back what I had lost.

blocks.label: Stacked — this week's shape
blocks.cue: Weight in one hand, thirty seconds a side. One line under load, nothing shoved sideways.

items.head: Shapes drill
items.sub: Two minutes, every day. This week's shape is stacked — weight in one hand, thirty seconds a side, nothing shoved sideways.

items.head: Three strength sessions
items.sub: One live, two on your own. The same six patterns, more load, three rounds.

items.head: Write every set as you go
items.sub: Between rounds, on the floor, sweating. Not at the end from memory.

items.head: The honest set
items.sub: Once this week. One movement, taken to two reps short of your form breaking. Box the number and date it.

items.head: Three walks
items.sub: Two at twenty-five minutes conversational, one at thirty with a hill. Time how long your breath takes to come back.

items.head: One long stretch
items.sub: Twenty minutes, week one's plus a low lunge, ninety seconds each side.

items.head: Draw the line
items.sub: A page, split down the middle. Left column, ten minutes. What you currently outsource because your body cannot or you do not trust it to.

items.head: Be petty and specific
items.sub: The water jugs, the top shelf, the second flight, the trip you did not take, the floor you do not sit on.

items.head: Right column
items.sub: Next to each one, who pays for it. Name the actual person, or write me if you paid in money or embarrassment or not going.

items.head: Circle three
items.sub: Only three. The three that would be gone if you were meaningfully stronger.

items.head: One sentence
items.sub: In eight weeks I want the water jugs off this list. Your version, specific enough that you would know if it happened.

items.head: Say it out loud
items.sub: I am allowed to be strong. If it catches in your throat, write down what it caught on. That is the week's real material.

blocks.text: She girds herself with strength and makes her arms strong.
blocks.why: Makes is a verb of training, and it sits in the middle of a chapter about a woman who chose a heavy load and carries it.

blocks.text: Bodily training is of some value.
blocks.why: Most of us have been running on a translation that says none.

items: Three strength sessions completed and written down set by set — the notebook is the proof, not the soreness
Something measurably heavier or longer than week one on at least two of the six patterns, and you can name which two
One honest set number, boxed and dated
Three walks logged, one with a climb, one recovery time in minutes and seconds
Seven daily logs, each with a number and an effort score
The ledger filled on both sides, three circled, one sentence at the bottom
The shapes drill, seven of seven
blocks.demo: Hold the stacked shape thirty seconds with a real weight in one hand, both sides, without the shoulder dropping or the hip shoving out — and say progressive overload back in one sentence without using either word.

week_list.title: The War, and Laying the Weapons Down
week_list.opening_line: You have been at war with your body for thirty years and you have never once seen the invoice.
week_list.stakes: Skip this and every pound of strength becomes a better weapon. You will punish yourself with excellent form. On the other side is one whole day without a single hostile thought about your own body — probably your first since middle school.
week_list.pull_quote: Surrender is not giving up on your body. It is taking your hands off the throat of it.

blocks.v: What has to be automatic first
Fourteen days kept. The twelfth rep that could not happen last Tuesday. Proof that load and repetition do what contempt never did. Something in your hands before the weapon goes down.
You cannot lay a weapon down until you have something else in your hands. If the last two weeks were patchy, repeat week two. This week will still be here and it will land four times harder.

blocks.title: The five weapons — find yours
rows: Not looking. Checking. Sideways, in one specific light, five to fifteen times a day
Every day begins with a verdict handed down by a bathroom
Insulting yourself first, out loud, so nobody else gets to
It works, which is the problem, and it costs you every single time
Food as owed, movement as payment. I'll have the bread but I'm walking tomorrow
A ledger running all day in which you are always slightly behind
The photo you stepped out of, the pool you did not get in, the dress with the tags on
The rooms you entered already braced, calculating where you rank
When I lose fifteen. The version of your life that starts when a number moves
Twenty years of rent on an apartment you never moved into

blocks.label: Hollow — this week's shape
blocks.cue: Held from the middle, eyes closed, with nobody telling you it looks right.

items.head: Shapes drill, eyes closed
items.sub: Two minutes, all four, every day, no mirror and no phone. This week's shape is hollow.

items.head: Two slow sessions
items.sub: Bodyweight only, three seconds down on everything. No load, no honest set, no numbers in the log.

items.head: One inside-the-body session
items.sub: Twenty-five minutes on the floor, no music with words. Long holds. Notice what it feels like from the inside.

items.head: Three walks
items.sub: Twenty-five to thirty minutes. At least one with no headphones. Whatever comes up in that silence is the assignment.

items.head: Sixty seconds of your hand
items.sub: Every day, resting on the part of your body you like least. Warm hand, breathing, no fixing and no assessing.

items.head: Film once, on day seven
items.sub: Ten seconds of the hollow, watched once. Most women are far closer than they feared.

blocks.title: The inner work — laying the weapons down

items.head: The age
items.sub: Forty minutes, alone, midweek, on a day you do not have to be anywhere after. Top of a blank page, write the number. Then one paragraph — where you were, who was there, what was said.

items.head: The weapons
items.sub: List yours. Use my five and add your private ones. Not I criticize myself but the exact mirror, the exact time of day, the exact angle.

items.head: The cost
items.sub: Next to each one, one thing it has actually taken from you. This part will hurt. Nobody lays down a weapon she thinks is working.

items.head: The verdict
items.sub: Write out the sentence handed down when you were eleven, in the voice it was said in. One line.

items.head: The appeal
items.sub: Underneath it, in your own hand, write who says it isn't so. Knit. On purpose. Wonderfully. Before any of them ever saw you.

items.head: The laying down
items.sub: Stand up. Say the verdict out loud once, then the finding out loud once. Then fold the page away, burn it safely outside, or date it and keep it in the front of the workbook. Decide before you start.

blocks.text: You knit me together in my mother's womb. I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
blocks.why: The making happened before anyone had an opinion, and wonderfully is the word chosen by someone looking straight at it.

blocks.text: Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you.
blocks.why: Paul is arguing against contempt for the body, not prescribing one — and if God lives here, the way you talk in fitting rooms is not discipline.

items: Seven daily logs, seven days of thirty minutes, and not a single number in any of them
Two slow bodyweight sessions, one floor session, three walks, one of them silent
The forty minutes done in one sitting, all six steps, verdict and finding both said out loud standing up
The weapons page dealt with — folded, burned, or dated and kept, and not left undecided
Seven days of the hand, sixty seconds each
A tally with a real total on it, and any number is a pass
The shapes drill seven of seven, eyes closed every time
blocks.demo: Put your body into all four shapes with your eyes shut from a standing start, nobody naming them, and hold the hollow twenty seconds without the low back lifting — checked on film afterward, not during.

blocks.v: Fresh grief, old material arriving with your whole body attached, or anything tangled around food belongs in a room with a licensed professional in it. That is not a cut corner and I will not pretend it is.

week_list.title: The Long Walk
week_list.opening_line: There is a whole category of things in your life that only answer to duration, and you have been going harder at every single one of them.
week_list.stakes: Skip this week and you stay a woman who can do hard things in bursts and cannot do a medium thing for a long time — the exact profile of everyone who has ever quit in month four. What you lose is the fourteenth month of a prayer nobody is admiring you for.
week_list.pull_quote: You cannot intensify a thing that only answers to duration. You can only still be walking at month nine.

blocks.v: What has to be automatic first
The mirror covered. Five weapons named in your own exact words. A tally with a real number on it. Somewhere to put the voice at minute twenty-six that is not agreement.
Without week three the hour is not a walk, it is a trial and you are the defendant. The count is what makes the hour survivable. You mark it and keep walking.

items.head: Four walks
items.sub: One long, three short. The table below is the spec. Slower than your ego wants, all four.

items.head: Two strength sessions
items.sub: Held at week two's load. No progression. You are spending the budget somewhere else on purpose.

items.head: Shapes drill, eyes open again
items.sub: Two minutes daily. This week's shape is stacked, and on the long walk it is an hour long — check jaw, shoulders and hands at minute twenty and minute forty-five.

items.head: One long stretch
items.sub: Twenty minutes with calves and feet added. Your feet did an hour of work. Pay them.

items.head: Check your shoes tonight
items.sub: Actually look at them. This is the week blisters end a lesson.

blocks.title: This week's walking — four walks, and what each one is for
rows: Sixty minutes minimum, conversational, no podcast for the first twenty and the last ten
Staying in something after the interesting part is over
Thirty minutes with a climb. Let the breath go short, then time how long it takes to settle
The slow system, and the only number that moves this early
Thirty minutes, mouth closed. If it opens, slow down until it closes
A pace governor you will have for life, and it costs nothing
Volume on your feet, which is the only input the slow system accepts

blocks.title: The inner work — the thing you're still waiting for

items.head: Before you go, five minutes
items.sub: Write one sentence. The thing you have asked God for that has not come. Not the polite version. Fold it and put it in your pocket.

items.head: Minute five
items.sub: Say it out loud, once, as a request. No softening clause tacked on the end of it.

items.head: Minutes six to twenty, no input
items.sub: Let it be boring. Every time you catch yourself strategizing, say the sentence again and go back to walking. You will do this eleven times and the catching is the exercise.

items.head: Minutes twenty to fifty
items.sub: Anything. Music if you want it. Look at things. Walk.

items.head: Minute thirty-eight
items.sub: Notice where you are. That is the whole instruction and you will be glad you looked.

items.head: Last ten minutes, no input again
items.sub: Carry one question and do not force it into words. What would I do this year if I knew the answer was still ten months out?

blocks.text: They shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
blocks.why: It descends, and the promise lands on the least impressive verb, which is the one your life is mostly made of.

blocks.text: Let us run with endurance the race that is set before us.
blocks.why: Endurance means staying under a load without collapsing, and nobody in Scripture is promised speed.

Three walks of thirty minutes, one with a climb and one nose-only
One recovery time written in seconds after the hill
Two strength sessions at last week's load, honest set included
The sentence written before the walk, said out loud at minute five, and written on the back of the same page when you got home
One paragraph about minute thirty-eight, not a summary of the walk
Seven daily logs with minutes on your feet and a breathing effort
The shapes drill seven of seven, twenty-eight days by Sunday
blocks.demo: The sixty unbroken minutes, conversational, with the prayer carried and not solved. It is binary. If you cut the hour to forty because you got bored, do the hour again this weekend before week five.

week_list.title: The Week It Falls Apart
week_list.opening_line: I scheduled this week. It is in my notes from a year ago, before I had ever met you, in my handwriting: week five is where it falls apart.
week_list.stakes: Skip it and you leave with the pattern you walked in with — perfect, perfect, perfect, gone — and the cut corner still sitting in the dark where you left it. A third of you will lose this program without ever missing a single day, because the freeze arrives before the miss does.
week_list.pull_quote: You did not quit because you missed a day. You quit because you agreed with the sentence.

blocks.v: I fell constantly. Every new skill, every time, for years. Hit the mat, get up, go again — and each fall handed me one piece of information toward executing it.
So know what a fall is here. Not a catastrophe. Not a lesson with a bow on it. The ordinary cost of attempting something you cannot do yet.
What has to be automatic first
An hour of boredom survived. Four weeks of days in the log. Twenty-nine kept days to weigh one missed one against. The miss stays what it is — data. Then the return, the next day, no speech.

blocks.label: Landing — this week's shape
blocks.cue: Ten off a low step, every day. Chest up, chin up, quiet feet, one second still at the bottom.

items.head: Landings, ten off a step
items.sub: Not five. A stair, a curb, a low bench. Quiet feet, one second still at the bottom.

items.head: The floor, rehearsed once
items.sub: Ten minutes, three movements, in whatever you are already wearing. Rehearsal, not workout.

items.head: Two strength sessions
items.sub: Back to progression. One rep per set or one small increment over week four.

items.head: Three walks
items.sub: Thirty minutes each. One of them is the repair walk.

items.head: Shapes drill, every day
items.sub: Two minutes — and on any day you miss the thirty minutes, you still do this. That is the whole week in one instruction.

items.head: One long stretch
items.sub: Twenty minutes on the floor, as week four.

Ten minutes, any room, the clothes you have on. Memorise it this week and you have it for twenty years.
The Six, three rounds — goblet squat ×11, RDL ×11, push-up at your hardest honest level ×8, row ×11, carry 50 sec a side, side plank 25 sec a side
Honest set once, number written and boxed

One of the three, taken the day after a miss or after your deliberate skip

Every single day, including the day it went wrong

blocks.v: The repair path

For the dread that arrives with nothing to point at: it is a bill, not a verdict. Go and read the log — it is the receipt. Back one rung, to the prerequisite. Four days until it costs no attention. Come back, and notice the dread went with the gap.

blocks.title: The inner work — the sentence and the script

items.head: Find the sentence
items.sub: The last time you broke a commitment to yourself — what were the exact words the next morning? In quotation marks, in the voice it arrives in. Most women find five to eight.

items.head: Date it
items.sub: How old is it? Where is the earliest you can remember thinking it, and was it about your body then?

items.head: Test it
items.sub: Cold, like an accountant, no charity. Five things you have actually finished, in writing. Then read the sentence again in the presence of that list.

items.head: Write the script
items.sub: Two sentences you will say the next morning after a miss. Mine is: That day's gone. Today's is at seven. Long is unusable.

items.head: Write the floor
items.sub: Which three movements, which room, which clothes. A floor you cannot locate on the day is not a floor.

items.head: Say it and record it
items.sub: Out loud ten times until it is smooth enough to use when you are tired and it is dark. Title the memo something you would open on a bad morning.

blocks.text: The righteous falls seven times and rises again.
blocks.why: It does not say she doesn't fall — seven falls sit inside the definition, and what distinguishes her is the rise count.

blocks.text: His mercies never come to an end. They are new every morning.
blocks.why: Written in a burned city with nothing resolved, which makes it a supply line and not a sentiment — Wednesday does not open in debt to Tuesday.

blocks.title: Done means
items: The ten-minute floor physically done at least once, and logged — not read, done
The floor written on a card, and the card in a physical place you can name out loud
The sentence written, in quotes, in the voice it arrives in
Five finished things listed — five, countable
A two-sentence script, written, said out loud, recorded
Either a deliberate skip logged as chosen and followed by an on-time session, or at least one four-word return entry
Seven daily logs, and any missed day followed by a return within one day
The shapes drill seven of seven, ten landings a day, including any day you missed the thirty minutes
blocks.demo: Say your two sentences out loud from memory with nothing in front of you, put your body through ten quiet landings off a step, and have either a deliberate skip or a four-word return sitting in your group feed where the room can see it.

blocks.title: Not every hard thing is a gap
blocks.v: Grief, illness, a body genuinely under-slept and under-fed, or old material arriving with your whole self attached is not a cut corner and does not get drilled at. That is the floor, and rest, and in some cases a licensed professional.

week_list.title: Being Seen
week_list.opening_line: You are the one who notices. You remember the surgery date, you catch the thing in her voice — and being the one who sees is how you have arranged never to be the one who is seen.
week_list.stakes: Skip this and the last five weeks were workouts you did alone in front of an audience you ignored, and the self you perform walks out of here intact and uncontradicted. A woman who cannot hold a sentence from a friend cannot hold an answer from God either.
week_list.pull_quote: A group where everybody reports success is a group that manufactures isolation.

blocks.v: Jeff could see in one rep what I could not feel in fifty. And it was easy to change once somebody else saw it. Easy. The seeing was the whole cost.

blocks.title: Where you need a spot this week

left.head: Go alone
items: The shapes with your eyes closed, drilled forty-two days
The walks
The honest set, because a voice at rep eight makes the number mine and not yours
The page nobody reads

right.head: Get an outside eye
items: Your hinge under load, which you cannot see and cannot feel
The deflection you use, which has a house version you have never once heard
What your face does at the heavier weight
The thing everyone who knows you has noticed and nobody has said

blocks.v: The right column is why you are in a room and not reading a book. Alone at nine at night, buy the eye elsewhere: film one set, send it to one woman.
What has to be automatic first
A floor and a script that exist. Something that actually went wrong. Four words posted where somebody saw them. Nothing left that needs an apology. Now you can be seen not-perfect.
Being seen at your best is not being seen. If five weeks have been immaculate and you skipped the deliberate miss, go and do it before you start this week. I am not joking and it is not a punishment.

blocks.label: Arch — this week's shape
blocks.cue: Thirty seconds, twice a day. Chest and thighs lifted, throat open, the whole front of you exposed.

items.head: Arch, held longer
items.sub: Thirty seconds instead of twenty, twice a day. Notice how much you want to shorten it.

items.head: Three strength sessions
items.sub: Four rounds now, up from three. Five to ten per cent more load, or two more reps, whichever your form will take.

items.head: The benchmark repeat
items.sub: Your honest set from week two — same movement, same version. Write the new number on the same line as the old one.

items.head: One session with somebody
items.sub: In person, on video, or on the phone with both of you moving at the same time and saying the count out loud. Not a recording. Simultaneous.

items.head: Three walks
items.sub: Thirty minutes. One of them with another woman, in real life or on the phone the whole way.

items.head: One long stretch
items.sub: Twenty minutes, as week four.

The pause is where it gets honest
RDL, heavier, three seconds on the way down
Long at the back of the legs, flat back, never sharp

Elbows past the ribs, back flat throughout

Hips lifted the whole time, not sagging at twenty

blocks.title: The inner work — seen and seeing

items.head: Open the tally page tonight
items.sub: Put the date on it. The drill starts tomorrow morning and runs all week.

items.head: Thank you, then three seconds
items.sub: Every time somebody says something good. Count them in your head. Then a mark, and one word for what your body did.

items.head: Write the real post
items.sub: Ten minutes. One day this week, told the way you would tell your closest friend, including the part you would normally cut.

items.head: Read it once and post it
items.sub: Once. The second reread is where you sand off the real part. Then close the app for an hour.

items.head: Pick two women
